beats: An automated agent kept crashing mid-task, twice in one week, with nothing to show for it.
Each time, its conversation history had quietly grown too large to think.
Now it watches itself: a systemd timer checks in every five minutes.
Like a whiteboard wiped clean before it overflows, it archives the old conversation and starts over, before failing, not after.
Both real crashes hit past 0.7 megabytes. The new threshold catches it at 0.25, twice as early.
